correctness.rationale: The statement concerns exact population mean projection widths of F_s=conv((1+s)K at +H/2,(1-s)K at -H/2), with compact full-dimensional origin-containing planar convex K and known H. For u=(sqrt(1-t²)v,t), t>=0, the support-max calculation gives w_s=a[(1+s)p+(1-s)q]+Ht+(2saq-Ht)_+, where p=h_K(v), q=h_K(-v). Averaging p-q over uniform v cancels the first-order term; the elementary hinge integral equals (b/2)atan(b/H) with b=2s q. This proves E(W_s-W_0)=s E[h_K(V)atan(2s h_K(V)/H)]. Compact-support moment determinacy of positive h² makes the entire response exactly equivalent to its support-value histogram; it does not reconstruct K. Pointwise convexity in the taper and reflection symmetry of the width distribution yield increasing-convex order, strict for strictly increasing convex tests; K=-K gives pointwise order. Independent direct support maxima and numerical hinge integrals on an asymmetric triangle at four s matched the formula. Numerics do not replace analytic proof.
residual_risks: The shape/orientation and finite-noise stability are explicitly not recovered; response uniqueness assumes H and centering known.
Quantitative monotonicity is in increasing-convex order for nonsymmetric bases, not a pointwise width comparison.

The even-moment readout and precise non-identifiability boundary are useful beyond basic convexity, despite no finite-sample or shape reconstruction theorem.
